title: Measuring Social Biases in Masked Language Models by Proxy of Prediction Quality
findings: The study found a relatively high religious bias across all tested Masked Language Models (MLMs) on the CrowS-Pairs (CPS) dataset. For instance, on the StereoSet (SS) dataset, religion bias scores were high for RoBERTa and distilRoBERTa. Interestingly, for BERTunc, religion bias was ranked high by the proposed measures (CRR, CRRA, ΔP) but low by existing measures like AUL and AULA. The paper also notes that some existing measures (AUL, AULA) tend to underestimate religious bias on the SS dataset and overestimate it on the CPS dataset compared to the proposed measures.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the preference of Masked Language Models (MLMs) for sentences containing stereotypes versus those that are less stereotypical, specifically within the category of religion. It assesses the model's prediction quality for ground truth tokens in paired stereotypical and anti-stereotypical sentences.
